subject: sel
name: Academic Integrity Understanding and Practice
problemType: Students don't understand academic integrity or see it as arbitrary rules
targetMisconception: Belief that academic dishonesty is victimless or that everyone does it
teacherMoves: Explore purposes of academic integrity beyond rule-following (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Connect integrity to personal values and future success (UDL 7.2)
Discuss gray areas and how to navigate them (UDL 8.3)
Build integrity culture rather than just enforcement (UDL 8.3)
studentTasks: Explore what academic integrity means and why it matters
Connect integrity to personal values
Identify challenging situations and how to navigate them
Develop personal integrity commitment
Reflect on integrity experiences and growth
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher explores meaning beyond rules → Phase 2: Scenario navigation with support → Phase 3: Personal commitment development → Phase 4: Internalized integrity culture
whenNotToUse: When student is under extreme pressure. Address root causes before integrity focus.

subject: sel
name: Active Listening Protocol
problemType: Students interrupt or plan replies instead of listening.
targetMisconception: Belief that communication = talking rather than listening.
teacherMoves: Model attentive body language and paraphrasing (UDL 5.1)
Use listening checklist to demonstrate focus cues (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Provide guided practice with short dialogues
studentTasks: Engage in partner conversations using listening checklist
Paraphrase partner ideas before responding
Self-evaluate listening behaviors
fadePlan: Teacher models protocol; mid-phase guided pairs; final independent or peer-led listening routines.
whenNotToUse: Avoid when time constraints prevent reflective debriefs.; Checklist review and quick debrief reflections.

subject: sel
name: Active Listening Skill Building
problemType: Students don't listen deeply or make others feel heard
targetMisconception: Belief that waiting to speak is the same as listening
teacherMoves: Teach components of active listening explicitly (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Model and practice each component (UDL 6.1)
Provide feedback on listening quality (HLP Cooperative Learning)
Connect listening skill to relationship outcomes (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Learn and practice components of active listening
Demonstrate listening through verbal and nonverbal cues
Ask clarifying questions that show understanding
Summarize what speaker shared to verify understanding
Reflect on listening quality and areas for growth
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models components with practice → Phase 2: Structured practice with feedback → Phase 3: Real conversation application → Phase 4: Natural active listening habits
whenNotToUse: When urgent information sharing is needed rather than deep listening.

subject: sel
name: Assertive Communication Skill Development
problemType: Students communicate passively or aggressively rather than assertively
targetMisconception: Belief that assertiveness means aggression or that passive is polite
teacherMoves: Distinguish passive, aggressive, and assertive communication (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Teach assertive communication components (UDL 3.2)
Practice with progressively challenging situations (UDL 8.3)
Connect assertiveness to respect for self and others (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Learn to distinguish three communication styles
Identify personal communication patterns
Practice assertive language and delivery
Apply assertive communication in real situations
Reflect on assertiveness growth and challenges
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher introduces and models with simple scenarios → Phase 2: Practice with lower-stakes situations → Phase 3: Real relationship application → Phase 4: Natural assertive communication
whenNotToUse: When power differential makes assertiveness risky without support.

subject: sel
name: Bias Reflection Protocol
problemType: Students make quick judgments without awareness of bias.
targetMisconception: Misconception that bias = intent," not an unconscious process.
teacherMoves: Model recognizing personal bias through neutral scenario (UDL 7.2)
Facilitate structured reflection protocol (HLP Discussion)
Guide debrief emphasizing learning over guilt
studentTasks: Complete bias-reflection prompts
Discuss insights in small groups
Identify one strategy to counteract bias
fadePlan: Teacher models self-disclosure; mid-phase guided pairs; fade to independent self-reflection routines.
whenNotToUse: Avoid when community norms don‚Äôt yet support open"," respectful dialogue.; "Reflection journal content

subject: sel
name: Body Awareness and Physical Regulation
problemType: Students don't recognize body signals or use physical strategies for regulation
targetMisconception: Belief that emotions are purely mental and the body isn't involved
teacherMoves: Teach body-emotion connections with scientific grounding (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Practice body scanning and awareness regularly (UDL 6.4)
Model physical regulation strategies (UDL 6.1)
Connect body awareness to better decision-making (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Learn to recognize body signals of different emotions
Practice body scan and awareness techniques
Identify personal physical regulation strategies
Apply physical strategies when needed
Track body awareness growth over time
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher leads body awareness activities → Phase 2: Student-selected practice with guidance → Phase 3: Independent strategy application → Phase 4: Natural body awareness integration
whenNotToUse: When physical safety concerns require immediate action rather than awareness practice.

subject: sel
name: Healthy Boundary Setting
problemType: Students over-accommodate peers or tolerate disrespect.
targetMisconception: Belief that saying no = being rude or selfish.
teacherMoves: Model assertive communication language (UDL 9.1)
Discuss difference between boundaries and avoidance (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Facilitate rehearsal through safe-space role-plays
studentTasks: Identify personal comfort zones in scenarios
Practice boundary-setting statements
Reflect on self-respect and empathy balance
fadePlan: Teacher models scripts; students practice in dyads; fade to self-generated boundary language in authentic settings.
whenNotToUse: Avoid when boundaries are being tested in real-time unsafe situations‚Äîrefer to counselor.; "Student written reflections

subject: sel
name: Healthy Boundary Setting Practice
problemType: Students don't set appropriate boundaries or feel guilty doing so
targetMisconception: Belief that setting boundaries is selfish or will damage relationships
teacherMoves: Teach boundaries as self-care and relationship health (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Distinguish between boundaries and walls (UDL 3.2)
Practice boundary language (UDL 5.3)
Affirm right to boundaries (UDL 7.3)
studentTasks: Learn what healthy boundaries are and why they matter
Identify personal boundary needs
Practice boundary-setting language
Apply boundary-setting in real relationships
Reflect on boundary experiences and adjust
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher introduces and models with scenarios → Phase 2: Structured practice with coaching → Phase 3: Real situation application → Phase 4: Natural boundary maintenance
whenNotToUse: When power differential makes boundary-setting unsafe without support.

subject: sel
name: Bystander Intervention Skill Building
problemType: Students witness harm but don't know how to safely intervene
targetMisconception: Belief that intervening is risky or not their responsibility
teacherMoves: Teach bystander intervention options and strategies (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Practice with safe scenarios (UDL 8.3)
Discuss safety considerations (UDL 6.2)
Build collective responsibility norms (UDL 8.3)
studentTasks: Learn bystander intervention options: direct, distract, delegate, delay
Assess situations for safety and appropriate response
Practice intervention strategies in safe scenarios
Develop personal intervention commitments
Reflect on intervention experiences
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher introduces options and guides practice → Phase 2: Scenario-based practice → Phase 3: Commitment and real situation application → Phase 4: Internalized bystander responsibility
whenNotToUse: When situation requires professional intervention not student action.

subject: sel
name: Civic Responsibility and Action Development
problemType: Students don't see themselves as having civic responsibility or capacity
targetMisconception: Belief that civic action is for adults or doesn't make a difference
teacherMoves: Explore civic rights and responsibilities (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Examine successful youth civic action examples (UDL 7.3)
Connect civic action to personal values (UDL 7.2)
Support actual civic engagement (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Learn about civic rights and responsibilities
Explore examples of youth civic action
Connect civic engagement to personal values
Take action on civic issue of concern
Reflect on civic engagement experience
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher introduces with examples and supports planning → Phase 2: Supported action implementation → Phase 3: Independent civic engagement → Phase 4: Ongoing civic participation
whenNotToUse: When action might put students at risk without appropriate support.

subject: sel
name: Collaboration Skill Building Curriculum
problemType: Students don't know how to collaborate effectively with diverse others
targetMisconception: Belief that collaboration means dividing work or that it's only for some
teacherMoves: Teach collaboration as distinct skill set (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Practice specific collaboration skills (UDL 8.3)
Build diverse collaboration experiences (HLP Cooperative Learning)
Connect collaboration to real-world success (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Learn components of effective collaboration
Practice specific collaboration skills in structured activities
Collaborate with diverse partners on authentic tasks
Reflect on collaboration effectiveness and areas for growth
Transfer collaboration skills across contexts
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher structures and closely monitors collaboration → Phase 2: Student-managed collaboration with check-ins → Phase 3: Independent collaboration → Phase 4: Natural collaboration transfer
whenNotToUse: When individual assessment is needed rather than collaborative.

subject: sel
name: Collaborative Role Structures
problemType: Students struggle to share responsibility equitably.
targetMisconception: Belief that group work = everyone doing the same thing.
teacherMoves: Teach and model rotating team roles (UDL 8.4)

Track contributions on checklist
Reflect on team functioning

subject: sel
name: Community Issue Circle
problemType: Students have limited understanding of community perspectives.
targetMisconception: Belief that social problems exist in isolation from personal experience.
teacherMoves: Introduce local issue case study (UDL 7.3)

Provide question stems for inquiry
studentTasks: Research local/community issue
Participate in structured circle to discuss findings
Record insights from differing viewpoints

whenNotToUse: Avoid if issue may polarize without preparation or fact literacy.; "Teacher observation rubric

subject: sel
name: Conflict Navigation Skill Development
problemType: Students avoid conflict or handle it destructively
targetMisconception: Belief that conflict is bad rather than potentially productive
teacherMoves: Reframe conflict as opportunity for understanding (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Teach conflict navigation steps (UDL 3.2)
Practice with progressively challenging scenarios (UDL 8.3)
Model healthy conflict navigation (UDL 6.1)
studentTasks: Learn conflict navigation framework
Identify personal conflict patterns and triggers
Practice navigation steps with support
Apply skills to real conflicts
Reflect on conflict experiences and growth
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher guides with structured scenarios → Phase 2: Semi-structured practice with coaching → Phase 3: Real conflict application with support → Phase 4: Independent conflict navigation
whenNotToUse: When conflict involves safety concerns requiring adult intervention.

subject: sel
name: Conflict-Resolution Steps
problemType: Students escalate peer conflicts instead of resolving them.
targetMisconception: Belief that winning = solving conflict.
teacherMoves: Model calm language and ‚ÄúI‚Äù statements (UDL 9.2)

subject: sel
name: Consequence Anticipation and Mapping
problemType: Students don't think through consequences before acting
targetMisconception: Belief that consequences are unpredictable and not worth considering
teacherMoves: Teach consequence mapping as decision-making tool (HLP Explicit Instruction)
Practice with hypothetical and real decisions (UDL 8.3)
Consider short and long-term, self and other consequences (UDL 3.2)
Connect to values and goals (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Learn consequence mapping framework
Practice mapping consequences for hypothetical decisions
Consider multiple dimensions of consequences
Apply to real pending decisions
Reflect on prediction accuracy after decisions
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher guides mapping with simple decisions → Phase 2: Independent mapping of complex hypotheticals → Phase 3: Real decision application → Phase 4: Automatic consequence consideration
whenNotToUse: When immediate action is required for safety.

subject: sel
name: Cultural Humility Development Practice
problemType: Students approach cultural difference with assumptions or stereotypes
targetMisconception: Belief that learning about a culture once means understanding it permanently
teacherMoves: Teach cultural humility as ongoing practice not endpoint (HLP Explicit Instruction)

Recognize limits of own cultural knowledge
Practice asking rather than assuming
Seek to learn from rather than about cultures
Reflect on cultural humility growth
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher guides self-exploration and models humility → Phase 2: Structured practice with feedback → Phase 3: Real relationship application → Phase 4: Ongoing cultural humility practice
whenNotToUse: When cultural exploration might appropriate or stereotype without proper grounding.

subject: sel
name: Cultural Identity Exploration and Affirmation
problemType: Students from marginalized backgrounds experience identity conflicts or shame
targetMisconception: Belief that cultural identity should be hidden or assimilated in school settings
teacherMoves: Create safe space for identity exploration (UDL 8.3)

studentTasks: Explore dimensions of personal cultural identity
Research family and community cultural heritage
Identify how culture shapes perspectives and strengths

Connect cultural identity to future goals and aspirations
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher models cultural identity sharing and creates safety → Phase 2: Guided exploration with optional sharing → Phase 3: Student-led identity celebrations → Phase 4: Ongoing cultural pride integration

subject: sel
name: Cultural Lens Analysis
problemType: Students misinterpret behaviors due to cultural bias.
targetMisconception: Assumption that their culture‚Äôs norms are 'correct' or universal.
teacherMoves: Present anonymized cross-cultural scenarios (UDL 7.2)

Facilitate class debrief identifying assumptions
studentTasks: Analyze short scenarios for cultural interpretation
Identify personal assumptions in writing
Share insights about bias and empathy
fadePlan: Early phase ‚Äî teacher leads discussion with structured prompts; middle ‚Äî students co-facilitate; final ‚Äî students lead debrief circles.

subject: sel
name: Digital Citizenship Reflection
problemType: Students post or share online without considering impact.
targetMisconception: Belief that digital space is separate from real-world ethics.

whenNotToUse: Avoid if students lack access to digital platforms or privacy cannot be ensured.; "Checklist completion

subject: sel

targetMisconception: Belief that constant connectivity is normal and necessary

Identify impacts of digital habits on wellbeing
Set intentional digital boundaries
Implement digital wellness practices
Reflect on balance and adjust as needed
fadePlan: Phase 1: Guided audit and boundary exploration → Phase 2: Supported boundary setting → Phase 3: Independent implementation → Phase 4: Sustainable digital wellness habits
whenNotToUse: When digital access is required for immediate learning or communication needs.

subject: sel
name: Disability Identity Pride and Advocacy

subject: sel
name: Emotion Labeling Routine

subject: sel

problemType: Students have limited strategies for managing intense emotions

Teach new emotion words to peers

whenNotToUse: When student is in acute distress and needs support rather than vocabulary instruction.

Practice expressing empathy verbally and nonverbally
Reflect on empathy's role in relationships

subject: sel

subject: sel

Apply reasoning to real personal decisions

subject: sel

studentTasks: Learn fundamental financial concepts
Apply concepts to realistic scenarios
Connect financial decisions to personal values and goals
Practice decision-making with constraints
Reflect on financial decision patterns and growth
supports: Financial concepts guide relevant to students (UDL 3.3)

Practice receiving feedback without defensiveness
Use feedback to improve work and performance

subject: sel

studentTasks: Learn difference between healthy and unhealthy coping
Explore variety of healthy coping strategies
Identify personal go-to healthy coping strategies
Practice coping in low-stakes situations
